status.en: 14 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 30% fewer than the week before, most of them in Tigray, Amhara and Addis Ababa.
status.nb: 14 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 30 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Tigray, Amhara og Addis Ababa.

summary.en: Mass killings of Orthodox Christians resumed in Oromia, with attackers killing at least 60 believers in two separate incidents. Violence in Gambella left 12 dead and more than 80 injured, according to MSF. Over 35,000 Ethiopians have fled across the border into Kenya, intensifying the humanitarian crisis. The UN mission in Somalia has concluded and the UN food programme has appointed a new head amid the renewed conflict. The UCDP recorded 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Massedrap på ortodokse kristne gjenopptok i Oromia, der angripere drepte minst 60 troende i to separate hendelser. Vold i Gambella førte til 12 døde og mer enn 80 sårede, ifølge MSF. Over 35 000 etiopiere har flyktet over grensen til Kenya, noe som forverrer den humanitære krisen. FN-misjonen i Somalia er avsluttet og FN-matprogrammet har utnevnt en ny leder midt i den fornyede konflikten. UCDP registrerte 2 824 drepte i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Fano insurgency
background.extract: The Fano insurgency is an armed conflict and insurgency in the Amhara Region of Ethiopia that began in April 2023 between the Fano militia and the Ethiopian government. The conflict started after the government attempted to dissolve the Amhara Special Forces and other regional forces as part of a plan to reform and centralize the country's security apparatus, and integrate them into the federal armed forces. This move led to protests and armed resistance by local forces under Fano.
